utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Ira, what still needs fixing for the repair drive, and how many volunteers do we actually have?

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: I haven’t heard a firm list yet, Mina, but the chatter at the market was bikes, lamps, and a couple of small appliances; volunteer count sounds like maybe six, though I’d want to confirm.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Can you confirm the six volunteers today, and I’ll ask around for the exact bike, lamp, and appliance count.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Hey Noah, I heard there’s a repair drive coming up—if folks need tools or a spare set of hands, I’m happy to pitch in.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh, that’s great, Gus—thanks. I might’ve missed the details, but I’ll ask around and point folks your way if they need help.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Perfect, thanks Noah—just let me know what they’re short on, and I can bring over a toolbox or help set up when the time comes.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Oh Pia, I was just about to ask you about the repair drive—have you heard what time folks are supposed to bring things over?

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: I haven’t heard a firm time yet, and that worries me a bit—we should pin it down before people start showing up with heavy things.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Absolutely, let’s not have people hauling lamps and chairs around all morning; I’ll ask around and spread the word as soon as we’ve got a proper time.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Hey Opal, I’m glad you brought up the repair drive—how can I help out?

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Thanks, Sam—could you help me map who’s bringing tools and where they’ll be dropped off? I want to keep the repair stations organized from the start.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Absolutely, I can make a simple list of who’s bringing what and set up drop-off spots by station so nothing gets mixed up.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Hey Uli, I’m helping get the word out about the repair drive—want me to swing by later with the details or pass them along now?

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: Now is okay, thanks. I may not be able to help much, but I’d like to know what’s needed.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Great, thanks Uli — they’re looking for folks to bring broken household items, help sort parts, or just spread the word. I’ll pass your name along as interested and make sure you get the time and place.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Hi Leo, I’m glad we could connect—I'd love to get the repair drive organized in a way that’s easy for everyone to pitch in.

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Sounds good, Rosa. Let’s keep it simple: pick a date, list the repairs, and ask neighbors to sign up for what they can handle.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: That sounds perfect, Leo—I'll draft a simple repair list and signup sheet, and we can choose a date that gives everyone enough notice.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: I’m glad to help with the repair drive, Dane—can you tell me what’s already been arranged and what still needs doing?

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Thanks, Hana — I’m a bit late to the details myself, but I know the collection table is planned for Saturday morning. I’m checking who has tools and who can cover sign-ups.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Got it—before I commit, do you know what time Saturday morning and whether you need me more for bringing tools or covering the sign-up table?

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: Hi Mara, I’m happy to help with the repair drive—do you know what time slots you still need covered around school pickup?

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: Thanks, Faye—that would be wonderful. I’m still sorting the schedule, but the slots around school pickup are usually about 2:30 to 4:00; would any part of that work for you?

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: Yes, I can cover 2:30 to 3:15 before I need to grab the kids—if that helps, put me down for that stretch.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Hi Jules, I’m still catching up through what folks have told me—what’s the latest on the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Hey Nell! We’re still gathering names and busted items, but there’s good momentum—Sam’s crew has tools, and I’m trying to connect them with Maya’s group for drop-off help.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: That sounds promising—if you hear where the drop-off list is being kept, could you point me to it so I can add anything neighbors mention to me?

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Hey Kira, I’m a bit swamped, but I can help with the repair drive if you give me the quick version.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Alright, quick version: we’re collecting broken small appliances and matching them with folks who can fix them. Can you confirm whether you’re available Saturday morning or just later in the day?

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Saturday morning’s tight for me, but I can help later in the day—just tell me where to show up.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: I haven’t heard much about the repair drive yet, Oren. What are folks hoping to fix first?

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Oh, right—the repair drive! I think folks were talking about starting with the broken porch steps and a few leaky gutters, though I may be forgetting one or two things.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: That sounds like a sensible start. Do you know who’s keeping the list, or should I ask around quietly?

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Hey Cleo, I heard there’s a repair drive coming up—do you know the plan yet? I can help spread the word once we’ve got the details.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: I’m still gathering the supply list, but I’ll check with the organizers today and let you know the time and what we need so you can spread the word.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Sounds good, Cleo—once you hear the time and supply list from the organizers, I’ll pass it along to everyone.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Hey Rey, I was just out running errands and heard there’s a repair drive going on—what’s the latest?

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: I’ve only heard bits and pieces so far, Ira—sounds like folks are gathering broken small appliances and bikes, but I haven’t gotten the full details yet.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Got it—if I hear a time or drop-off spot while I’m out, I’ll pass it along.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Oh, the repair drive—right, Vik, thanks for reminding me. I’d be happy to help, though you may need to tell me again what time we’re starting.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Great, thanks Oren — I’ll check the exact start time and circle back so I don’t tell you wrong.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Thanks, Vik, I appreciate it. I’ll keep the day free and wait for your note about the time.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh hey Leo, I might be a little out of the loop—what’s the latest with the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: We’re collecting broken small appliances Saturday morning at the community shed. If you’ve got anything to fix or spare tools, bring them by.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Got it, Saturday morning at the shed—I’ll check my garage for any busted appliances and maybe a spare toolkit.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Hey Eli, I’ve got a few spare tools I can lend for the repair drive if that’d help. What are folks needing most?

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: That would help a lot, Gus. I think we most need screwdrivers, pliers, and a good socket set, but I’ll make a clear list before folks start dropping things off.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Perfect, I’ve got all three I can bring by once you’ve got the list. Just let me know if you need extension cords or a work light too.

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: Hi Quinn, I’m glad we’re talking about the repair drive—what still needs sorting out so we can help folks bring things in?

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Hi Mara! I think we still need to pin down drop-off times, a sign-up list for volunteers, and a quick way to spread the word so folks know what items to bring.

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: That sounds right; I can draft a volunteer sign-up sheet today, and we can pick a couple of clear drop-off windows that won’t crowd the sidewalk.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Hey Opal, I was thinking the repair drive could be a great way to bring a few different neighbor groups together. What kind of help do you need most right now?

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Right now I mostly need a clear list of where volunteers and tools will be stationed, so nobody overlaps or gets missed. If you can help coordinate which groups are covering which spots, that would be a big help.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Absolutely, I can do that—send me the spots you already have in mind, and I’ll start matching each one with a group and any tools they can bring.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Hi Cleo, I’m glad we could talk—I'm pulling together the repair drive details and would love your help figuring out what the block needs most.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: Absolutely, Rosa—I can help take stock. Let’s start with the basics: tools, patch materials, batteries, and anything folks have already said they’re short on.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: That’s perfect, Cleo—I'll make a checklist for those categories, and if you can ask around about the most urgent fixes, we can match supplies to real needs.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Hi Mina, I’m still catching up on the repair drive—what have you heard so far?

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Not much yet—who’s organizing it, and what repairs are they asking people to bring in?

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: I’m not sure yet—I’ve only heard bits from neighbors, so I was hoping you might know who’s coordinating it or where the sign-up sheet is.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Hey Faye, I caught something about a repair drive—what’s the quick version of what you need from me?

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: We’re collecting broken small items after school Friday, and I mostly need you to help at the sign-in table from 3:15 to 4 if that works.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Yep, I can do 3:15 to 4 at the sign-in table—just point me where to be Friday.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Hey Kira, I’d be happy to help with the repair drive—what still needs doing?

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: That’s good to hear, Sam, but can you confirm you’re definitely available this weekend before I put your name down?

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Yes, I’m definitely available this weekend—go ahead and put my name down.
